entry.title: Solving LLM Hallucination via Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | robw.fyi | discussion

LLMs often generate confidence scores as linguistic patterns rather than mathematical measurements, a phenomenon that contributes to hallucinations. Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD) mitigates this by training models to output probability distributions that align with actual empirical outcomes. This ensures that a model's stated certainty reflects its true likelihood of being correct.

Calibrated probabilities allow model outputs to be integrated into mathematical frameworks like the Kelly criterion to calculate optimal risk. While closed-source models may struggle to adapt their calibration to specific new domains, users can post-train open-source models like Laya with RLCD to create reliable, mathematical control signals for automated or autonomous systems.

The system establishes a launch-week baseline and conducts daily tests for 30 days to provide a high-confidence comparison against a control arm. By pinning specific CLI versions and employing a structured sampling protocol, the rig aims to differentiate between platform-wide infrastructure shifts and specific model degradation.
